newsitem.title: ITALY: Cancelled strike still snarls Italian airports.
newsitem.headline: Cancelled strike still snarls Italian airports.

text.p: Italian air traffic controllers called off plans for an eight-hour national strike on Wednesday after late-night talks with the government but travel was still disrupted, airport officials said.
The controllers' unions said they had decided to cancel the strike after an accord was signed in the presence of Transport Minister Claudio Burlando in the early hours of Wednesday morning.
The last-minute truce meant authorities were unable to inform passengers that services would run as normal.

Officials at Rome's Fiumicino international airport said it was deserted on Wednesday morning as many passengers either did not know the strike had been called off or had already made alternative travel arrangements.
The national flag carrier Alitalia said in a statement normal services would resume on Thursday but it was not immediately known if a strike planned for May 30 would go ahead.

The unions said the agreement with the government set the terms for a future meeting between the parties to settle long-running contract disputes which have brought air services to a standstill on a number of occasions this year.
Air travel is just one of the many transport sectors to be hit by a wave of recent strike action.

Local public transport unions called a one-day national strike earlier this week which forced commuters in Rome and other big centres to find alternative means of transport. Some railway unions plan industrial action for June 1.
Small ferry pilots' unions were on strike on Wednesday.
